params.name: custom-attribute-definition-key
params.description: The identifier of the custom attribute definition and its corresponding custom attributes. This value can be a simple key, which is the key that is provided when the custom attribute definition is created, or a qualified key, if the requesting application is not the definition owner. The qualified key consists of the application ID of the custom attribute definition owner followed by the simple key that was provided when the definition was created. It has the format application_id:simple key. The value for a simple key can contain up to 60 alphanumeric characters, periods (.), underscores (_), and hyphens (-). On writes, this field must be set to the latest version. Stale writes are rejected. This field can also be used to enforce strong consistency for reads. tools.name: catalog_batch-delete-objects
tools.description: Deletes a set of [CatalogItem](entity:CatalogItem)s based on the provided list of target IDs and returns a set of successfully deleted IDs in the response. Deletion is a cascading event such that all children of the targeted object are also deleted. For example, deleting a CatalogItem will also delete all of its [CatalogItemVariation](entity:CatalogItemVariation) children. `BatchDeleteCatalogObjects` succeeds even if only a portion of the targeted IDs can be deleted. The response will only include IDs that were actually deleted. To ensure consistency, only one delete request is processed at a time per seller account. While one (batch or non-batch) delete request is being processed, other (batched and non-batched) delete requests are rejected with the `429` error code. Required: object_ids.

params.name: object_ids
params.description: The IDs of the CatalogObjects to be deleted. When an object is deleted, other objects in the graph that depend on that object will be deleted as well (for example, deleting a CatalogItem will delete its CatalogItemVariation.

tools.name: catalog_batch-retrieve-objects
tools.description: Returns a set of objects based on the provided ID. Each [CatalogItem](entity:CatalogItem) returned in the set includes all of its child information including: all of its [CatalogItemVariation](entity:CatalogItemVariation) objects, references to its [CatalogModifierList](entity:CatalogModifierList) objects, and the ids of any [CatalogTax](entity:CatalogTax) objects that apply to it. Required: object_ids. Optional: catalog_version, include_category_path_to_root, include_deleted_objects (plus 1 more).

params.name: catalog_version
params.description: The specific version of the catalog objects to be included in the response. This allows you to retrieve historical versions of objects. The specified version value is matched against the [CatalogObject](entity:CatalogObject)s' `version` attribute. If not included, results will be from the current version of the catalog.

params.name: include_category_path_to_root
params.description: Specifies whether or not to include the `path_to_root` list for each returned category instance. The `path_to_root` list consists of `CategoryPathToRootNode` objects and specifies the path that starts with the immediate parent category of the returned category and ends with its root category. If the returned category is a top-level category, the `path_to_root` list is empty and is not returned in the response payload.

params.name: include_deleted_objects
params.description: Indicates whether to include (`true`) or not (`false`) in the response deleted objects, namely, those with the `is_deleted` attribute set to `true`.

params.name: include_related_objects
params.description: If `true`, the response will include additional objects that are related to the requested objects. Related objects are defined as any objects referenced by ID by the results in the `objects` field of the response. These objects are put in the `related_objects` field. Setting this to `true` is helpful when the objects are needed for immediate display to a user. This process only goes one level deep. Objects referenced by the related objects will not be included. For example, if the `objects` field of the response contains a CatalogItem, its associated CatalogCategory objects, CatalogTax objects, CatalogImage objects and CatalogModifierLists will be returned in the `related_objects` field of the response. If the `objects` field of the response contains a CatalogItemVariation, its parent CatalogItem will be returned in the `related_objects` field of the response. Default value: `false`

params.name: object_ids
params.description: The IDs of the CatalogObjects to be retrieved.

tools.name: catalog_batch-upsert-objects
tools.description: Creates or updates up to 10,000 target objects based on the provided list of objects. The target objects are grouped into batches and each batch is inserted/updated in an all-or-nothing manner. If an object within a batch is malformed in some way, or violates a database constraint, the entire batch containing that item will be disregarded. However, other batches in the same request may still succeed. Each batch may contain up to 1,000 objects, and batches will be processed in order as long as the total object count for the request (items, variations, modifier lists, discounts, and taxes) is no more than 10,000. This endpoint uses full-replacement semantics. The client must send the complete object, and any field absent from the request is interpreted as an intentional clear. This logic applies to nested objects as well. For example, omitting inlined children like variations will delete them. To ensure consistency, only one update request is processed at a time per seller account. While one (batch or non-batch) update request is being processed, other (batched and non-batched) update requests are rejected with the `429` error code. Prefer batching related changes into a single call rather than issuing many small writes, since each write acquires the lock separately and parallel writes to the same seller will contend with each other, producing `429` errors. Required: batches, idempotency_key. Returns the new BatchUpsertCatalogObjectsResponse.

params.name: batches
params.description: A batch of CatalogObjects to be inserted/updated atomically. The objects within a batch will be inserted in an all-or-nothing fashion, i.e., if an error occurs attempting to insert or update an object within a batch, the entire batch will be rejected. However, an error in one batch will not affect other batches within the same request. For each object, its `updated_at` field is ignored and replaced with a current [timestamp](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/build-basics/working-with-dates), and its `is_deleted` field must not be set to `true`. To modify an existing object, supply its ID. To create a new object, use an ID starting with `#`. These IDs may be used to create relationships between an object and attributes of other objects that reference it. For example, you can create a CatalogItem with ID `#ABC` and a CatalogItemVariation with its `item_id` attribute set to `#ABC` in order to associate the CatalogItemVariation with its parent CatalogItem. Any `#`-prefixed IDs are valid only within a single atomic batch, and will be replaced by server-generated IDs. Each batch may contain up to 1,000 objects. The total number of objects across all batches for a single request may not exceed 10,000. If either of these limits is violated, an error will be returned and no objects will be inserted or updated.

params.name: idempotency_key
params.description: A value you specify that uniquely identifies this request among all your requests. A common way to create a valid idempotency key is to use a Universally unique identifier (UUID). If you're unsure whether a particular request was successful, you can reattempt it with the same idempotency key without worrying about creating duplicate objects. See [Idempotency](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/build-basics/common-api-patterns/idempotency) for more information.

params.description: An optional case-insensitive, comma-separated list of object types to retrieve. The valid values are defined in the [CatalogObjectType](entity:CatalogObjectType) enum, for example, `ITEM`, `ITEM_VARIATION`, `CATEGORY`, `DISCOUNT`, `TAX`, `MODIFIER`, `MODIFIER_LIST`, `IMAGE`, etc. If this is unspecified, the operation returns objects of all the top level types at the version of the Square API used to make the request. Object types that are nested onto other object types are not included in the defaults. At the current API version the default object types are: ITEM, CATEGORY, TAX, DISCOUNT, MODIFIER_LIST, PRICING_RULE, PRODUCT_SET, TIME_PERIOD, MEASUREMENT_UNIT, SUBSCRIPTION_PLAN, ITEM_OPTION, CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTE_DEFINITION, QUICK_AMOUNT_SETTINGS.

params.name: catalog_version
params.description: The specific version of the catalog objects to be included in the response. This allows you to retrieve historical versions of objects. The specified version value is matched against the [CatalogObject](entity:CatalogObject)s' `version` attribute. If not included, results will be from the current version of the catalog.

tools.name: catalog_retrieve-object
tools.description: Returns a single [CatalogItem](entity:CatalogItem) as a [CatalogObject](entity:CatalogObject) based on the provided ID. The returned object includes all of the relevant [CatalogItem](entity:CatalogItem) information including: [CatalogItemVariation](entity:CatalogItemVariation) children, references to its [CatalogModifierList](entity:CatalogModifierList) objects, and the ids of any [CatalogTax](entity:CatalogTax) objects that apply to it. Required: object_id. Optional: include_related_objects (default: false), catalog_version, include_category_path_to_root (default: false).

params.name: object_id
params.description: The object ID of any type of catalog objects to be retrieved.

params.name: include_related_objects
params.description: If `true`, the response will include additional objects that are related to the requested objects. Related objects are defined as any objects referenced by ID by the results in the `objects` field of the response. These objects are put in the `related_objects` field. Setting this to `true` is helpful when the objects are needed for immediate display to a user. This process only goes one level deep. Objects referenced by the related objects will not be included. For example, if the `objects` field of the response contains a CatalogItem, its associated CatalogCategory objects, CatalogTax objects, CatalogImage objects and CatalogModifierLists will be returned in the `related_objects` field of the response. If the `objects` field of the response contains a CatalogItemVariation, its parent CatalogItem will be returned in the `related_objects` field of the response. Default value: `false`

params.name: catalog_version
params.description: Requests objects as of a specific version of the catalog. This allows you to retrieve historical versions of objects. The value to retrieve a specific version of an object can be found in the version field of [CatalogObject](entity:CatalogObject)s. If not included, results will be from the current version of the catalog.

params.name: include_category_path_to_root
params.description: Specifies whether or not to include the `path_to_root` list for each returned category instance. The `path_to_root` list consists of `CategoryPathToRootNode` objects and specifies the path that starts with the immediate parent category of the returned category and ends with its root category. If the returned category is a top-level category, the `path_to_root` list is empty and is not returned in the response payload.

tools.name: catalog_search-items
tools.description: Searches for catalog items or item variations by matching supported search attribute values, including custom attribute values, against one or more of the specified query filters. This (`SearchCatalogItems`) endpoint differs from the [SearchCatalogObjects](api-endpoint:Catalog-SearchCatalogObjects) endpoint in the following aspects: - `SearchCatalogItems` can only search for items or item variations, whereas `SearchCatalogObjects` can search for any type of catalog objects. - `SearchCatalogItems` supports the custom attribute query filters to return items or item variations that contain custom attribute values, where `SearchCatalogObjects` does not. - `SearchCatalogItems` does not support the `include_deleted_objects` filter to search for deleted items or item variations, whereas `SearchCatalogObjects` does. - The both endpoints use different call conventions, including the query filter formats. Optional: archived_state, category_ids, cursor (plus 7 more). Returns the new SearchCatalogItemsResponse.

params.name: archived_state
params.description: Defines the values for the `archived_state` query expression used in [SearchCatalogItems](api-endpoint:Catalog-SearchCatalogItems) to return the archived, not archived or either type of catalog items.

params.name: category_ids
params.description: The category id query expression to return items containing the specified category IDs.

params.name: cursor
params.description: The pagination token, returned in the previous response, used to fetch the next batch of pending results.

params.name: custom_attribute_filters
params.description: The customer-attribute filter to return items or item variations matching the specified custom attribute expressions. A maximum number of 10 custom attribute expressions are supported in a single call to the [SearchCatalogItems](api-endpoint:Catalog-SearchCatalogItems) endpoint.

params.name: enabled_location_ids
params.description: The enabled-location query expression to return items and item variations having specified enabled locations.

params.name: limit
params.description: The maximum number of results to return per page. The default value is 100.

params.name: product_types
params.description: The product types query expression to return items or item variations having the specified product types.

params.name: sort_order
params.description: The order (e.g., chronological or alphabetical) in which results from a request are returned.

params.name: stock_levels
params.description: The stock-level query expression to return item variations with the specified stock levels. See [SearchCatalogItemsRequestStockLevel](#type-searchcatalogitemsrequeststocklevel) for possible values

params.name: text_filter
params.description: The text filter expression to return items or item variations containing specified text in the `name`, `description`, or `abbreviation` attribute value of an item, or in the `name`, `sku`, or `upc` attribute value of an item variation.

tools.name: catalog_search-objects
tools.description: Searches for [CatalogObject](entity:CatalogObject) of any type by matching supported search attribute values, excluding custom attribute values on items or item variations, against one or more of the specified query filters. This (`SearchCatalogObjects`) endpoint differs from the [SearchCatalogItems](api-endpoint:Catalog-SearchCatalogItems) endpoint in the following aspects: - `SearchCatalogItems` can only search for items or item variations, whereas `SearchCatalogObjects` can search for any type of catalog objects. - `SearchCatalogItems` supports the custom attribute query filters to return items or item variations that contain custom attribute values, where `SearchCatalogObjects` does not. - `SearchCatalogItems` does not support the `include_deleted_objects` filter to search for deleted items or item variations, whereas `SearchCatalogObjects` does. - The both endpoints have different call conventions, including the query filter formats. The `object_types` parameter is specified as a list of [CatalogObjectType](entity:CatalogObjectType) values. Always specify `object_types` explicitly. When upgrading to a newer API version, omitting `object_types` may cause new object types to appear in results that were not returned under the previous version. Optional: begin_time, cursor, include_category_path_to_root (plus 5 more). Returns the new SearchCatalogObjectsResponse.

params.name: begin_time
params.description: Return objects modified after this [timestamp](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/build-basics/working-with-dates), in RFC 3339 format, e.g., `2016-09-04T23:59:33.123Z`. The timestamp is exclusive - objects with a timestamp equal to `begin_time` will not be included in the response.

params.name: cursor
params.description: The pagination cursor returned in the previous response. Leave unset for an initial request. See [Pagination](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/build-basics/common-api-patterns/pagination) for more information.

params.name: include_category_path_to_root
params.description: Specifies whether or not to include the `path_to_root` list for each returned category instance. The `path_to_root` list consists of `CategoryPathToRootNode` objects and specifies the path that starts with the immediate parent category of the returned category and ends with its root category. If the returned category is a top-level category, the `path_to_root` list is empty and is not returned in the response payload. If `include_category_path_to_root` is `true`, then the `include_deleted_objects` request parameter must be `false`. Both properties cannot be `true` at the same time.

params.name: include_deleted_objects
params.description: If `true`, deleted objects will be included in the results. Defaults to `false`. Deleted objects will have their `is_deleted` field set to `true`. If `include_deleted_objects` is `true`, then the `include_category_path_to_root` request parameter must be `false`. Both properties cannot be `true` at the same time.

params.name: include_related_objects
params.description: If `true`, the response will include additional objects that are related to the requested objects. Related objects are objects that are referenced by object ID by the objects in the response. This is helpful if the objects are being fetched for immediate display to a user. This process only goes one level deep. Objects referenced by the related objects will not be included. For example: If the `objects` field of the response contains a CatalogItem, its associated CatalogCategory objects, CatalogTax objects, CatalogImage objects and CatalogModifierLists will be returned in the `related_objects` field of the response. If the `objects` field of the response contains a CatalogItemVariation, its parent CatalogItem will be returned in the `related_objects` field of the response. Default value: `false`

params.name: limit
params.description: A limit on the number of results to be returned in a single page. The limit is advisory - the implementation may return more or fewer results. If the supplied limit is negative, zero, or is higher than the maximum limit of 1,000, it will be ignored.

params.name: object_types
params.description: The desired set of object types to appear in the search results. If this is unspecified, the operation returns objects of all the top level types at the version of the Square API used to make the request. Object types that are nested onto other object types are not included in the defaults. At the current API version the default object types are: ITEM, CATEGORY, TAX, DISCOUNT, MODIFIER_LIST, PRICING_RULE, PRODUCT_SET, TIME_PERIOD, MEASUREMENT_UNIT, SUBSCRIPTION_PLAN, ITEM_OPTION, CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTE_DEFINITION, QUICK_AMOUNT_SETTINGS. Note that if you wish for the query to return objects belonging to nested types (i.e., COMPONENT, IMAGE, ITEM_OPTION_VAL, ITEM_VARIATION, or MODIFIER), you must explicitly include all the types of interest in this field.

params.name: query-exact-query-attribute-name
params.description: The name of the attribute to be searched. Matching of the attribute name is exact.

params.name: query-exact-query-attribute-value
params.description: The desired value of the search attribute. Matching of the attribute value is case insensitive and can be partial. For example, if a specified value of 'sma', objects with the named attribute value of 'Small', 'small' are both matched.

params.name: query-item-variations-for-item-option-values-query
params.description: A query expression to return item variations (of the [CatalogItemVariation](entity:CatalogItemVariation) type) that contain all of the specified `CatalogItemOption` IDs.

params.name: query-items-for-item-options-query-item-option-ids
params.description: A set of `CatalogItemOption` IDs to be used to find associated `CatalogItem`s. All Items that contain all of the given Item Options (in any order) will be returned.

params.name: query-items-for-modifier-list-query-modifier-list-ids
params.description: A set of `CatalogModifierList` IDs to be used to find associated `CatalogItem`s.

params.name: query-items-for-tax-query-tax-ids
params.description: A set of `CatalogTax` IDs to be used to find associated `CatalogItem`s.

params.name: query-prefix-query-attribute-name
params.description: The name of the attribute to be searched.

params.name: query-prefix-query-attribute-prefix
params.description: The desired prefix of the search attribute value.

params.name: query-range-query-attribute-max-value
params.description: The desired maximum value for the search attribute (inclusive).

params.name: query-range-query-attribute-min-value
params.description: The desired minimum value for the search attribute (inclusive).

params.name: query-range-query-attribute-name
params.description: The name of the attribute to be searched.

params.name: query-set-query-attribute-name
params.description: The name of the attribute to be searched. Matching of the attribute name is exact.

params.name: query-set-query-attribute-values
params.description: The desired values of the search attribute. Matching of the attribute values is exact and case insensitive. A maximum of 250 values may be searched in a request.

params.name: query-sorted-attribute-query-attribute-name
params.description: The attribute whose value is used as the sort key.

params.name: query-sorted-attribute-query-initial-attribute-value
params.description: The first attribute value to be returned by the query. Ascending sorts will return only objects with this value or greater, while descending sorts will return only objects with this value or less. If unset, start at the beginning (for ascending sorts) or end (for descending sorts).

params.name: query-sorted-attribute-query-sort-order
params.description: The order (e.g., chronological or alphabetical) in which results from a request are returned.

params.name: query-text-query-keywords
params.description: A list of 1, 2, or 3 search keywords. Keywords with fewer than 3 alphanumeric characters are ignored.

tools.name: catalog_update-image

tools.name: catalog_upsert-object
tools.description: Creates a new or updates the specified [CatalogObject](entity:CatalogObject). This endpoint uses full-replacement semantics. The client must send the complete object, and any field absent from the request is interpreted as an intentional clear. This logic applies to nested objects as well. For example, omitting inlined children like variations will delete them. To ensure consistency, only one update request is processed at a time per seller account. While one (batch or non-batch) update request is being processed, other (batched and non-batched) update requests are rejected with the `429` error code. Required: idempotency_key, object. Returns the new UpsertCatalogObjectResponse.

params.name: idempotency_key
params.description: A value you specify that uniquely identifies this request among all your requests. A common way to create a valid idempotency key is to use a Universally unique identifier (UUID). If you're unsure whether a particular request was successful, you can reattempt it with the same idempotency key without worrying about creating duplicate objects. See [Idempotency](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/build-basics/common-api-patterns/idempotency) for more information.

params.name: object

tools.name: customers_bulk-create

Each key is an [idempotency key](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/build-basics/common-api-patterns/idempotency) that uniquely identifies the create request. Each value contains the customer data used to create the customer profile.

tools.description: Retrieves multiple customer profiles. This endpoint takes a list of customer IDs and returns a map of responses. Required: customer_ids.

params.name: customer_ids

tools.name: customers_bulk-update
tools.description: Updates multiple customer profiles. This endpoint takes a map of individual update requests and returns a map of responses. Required: customers.

params.name: customers
params.description: A map of 1 to 100 individual update requests, represented by `customer ID: { customer data }` key-value pairs. Each key is the ID of the [customer profile](entity:Customer) to update. To update a customer profile that was created by merging existing profiles, provide the ID of the newly created profile. Each value contains the updated customer data. Only new or changed fields are required. To add or update a field, specify the new value. To remove a field, specify `null`.

tools.name: customers_bulk-upsert-custom-attributes
tools.description: Creates or updates [custom attributes](entity:CustomAttribute) for customer profiles as a bulk operation. Use this endpoint to set the value of one or more custom attributes for one or more customer profiles. A custom attribute is based on a custom attribute definition in a Square seller account, which is created using the [CreateCustomerCustomAttributeDefinition](api-endpoint:CustomerCustomAttributes-CreateCustomerCustomAttributeDefinition) endpoint. This `BulkUpsertCustomerCustomAttributes` endpoint accepts a map of 1 to 25 individual upsert requests and returns a map of individual upsert responses. Each upsert request has a unique ID and provides a customer ID and custom attribute. Each upsert response is returned with the ID of the corresponding request. To create or update a custom attribute owned by another application, the `visibility` setting must be `VISIBILITY_READ_WRITE_VALUES`. Note that seller-defined custom attributes (also known as custom fields) are always set to `VISIBILITY_READ_WRITE_VALUES`. Required: values.

params.name: values
params.description: A map containing 1 to 25 individual upsert requests. For each request, provide an arbitrary ID that is unique for this `BulkUpsertCustomerCustomAttributes` request and the information needed to create or update a custom attribute.

tools.name: customers_create
tools.description: Creates a new customer for a business. params.name: address-postal-code
params.description: The address's postal code. For a full list of field meanings by country, see [Working with Addresses](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/build-basics/working-with-addresses).

params.name: address-sublocality

tools.name: customers_create-custom-attribute-definition
tools.description: Creates a customer-related [custom attribute definition](entity:CustomAttributeDefinition) for a Square seller account. Use this endpoint to define a custom attribute that can be associated with customer profiles. A custom attribute definition specifies the `key`, `visibility`, `schema`, and other properties for a custom attribute. After the definition is created, you can call [UpsertCustomerCustomAttribute](api-endpoint:CustomerCustomAttributes-UpsertCustomerCustomAttribute) or [BulkUpsertCustomerCustomAttributes](api-endpoint:CustomerCustomAttributes-BulkUpsertCustomerCustomAttributes) to set the custom attribute for customer profiles in the seller's Customer Directory. Sellers can view all custom attributes in exported customer data, including those set to `VISIBILITY_HIDDEN`. Required: custom_attribute_definition. Optional: idempotency_key. Returns array of Error.

params.name: custom-attribute-definition-created-at
params.description: The timestamp that indicates when the custom attribute definition was created, in RFC 3339 format.

params.name: custom-attribute-definition-description
params.description: Seller-oriented description of the custom attribute definition, including any constraints that the seller should observe. May be displayed as a tooltip in Square UIs. This field is required if the `visibility` field is `VISIBILITY_READ_ONLY` or `VISIBILITY_READ_WRITE_VALUES`.

params.name: custom-attribute-definition-key
params.description: The identifier of the custom attribute definition and its corresponding custom attributes. This value can be a simple key, which is the key that is provided when the custom attribute definition is created, or a qualified key, if the requesting application is not the definition owner. The qualified key consists of the application ID of the custom attribute definition owner followed by the simple key that was provided when the definition was created. It has the format application_id:simple key. The value for a simple key can contain up to 60 alphanumeric characters, periods (.), underscores (_), and hyphens (-). This field can not be changed after the custom attribute definition is created. This field is required when creating a definition and must be unique per application, seller, and resource type.

params.name: custom-attribute-definition-name
params.description: The name of the custom attribute definition for API and seller-facing UI purposes. The name must be unique within the seller and application pair. This field is required if the `visibility` field is `VISIBILITY_READ_ONLY` or `VISIBILITY_READ_WRITE_VALUES`.

params.name: custom-attribute-definition-schema
params.description: The JSON schema for the custom attribute definition, which determines the data type of the corresponding custom attributes. For more information, see [Custom Attributes Overview](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/devtools/customattributes/overview). This field is required when creating a definition.

params.name: custom-attribute-definition-updated-at
params.description: The timestamp that indicates when the custom attribute definition was created or most recently updated, in RFC 3339 format.

params.name: custom-attribute-definition-version
params.description: Read only. The current version of the custom attribute definition. The value is incremented each time the custom attribute definition is updated. When updating a custom attribute definition, you can provide this field and specify the current version of the custom attribute definition to enable [optimistic concurrency](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/build-basics/common-api-patterns/optimistic-concurrency). On writes, this field must be set to the latest version. Stale writes are rejected. This field can also be used to enforce strong consistency for reads. For more information about strong consistency for reads, see [Custom Attributes Overview](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/devtools/customattributes/overview).

params.name: custom-attribute-definition-visibility
params.description: The level of permission that a seller or other applications requires to view this custom attribute definition. The `Visibility` field controls who can read and write the custom attribute values and custom attribute definition.

params.name: idempotency_key

tools.name: inventory_create-adjustment-reason
tools.description: Creates a custom inventory adjustment reason. Required: adjustment_reason, idempotency_key. Returns array of Error.

params.name: adjustment-reason-created-at
params.description: An RFC 3339-formatted timestamp that indicates when the custom adjustment reason was created. This field is empty for standard adjustment reasons.

params.name: adjustment-reason-direction
params.description: Direction

params.name: adjustment-reason-id-custom-reason-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the custom adjustment reason. This field is only set when `type` is `CUSTOM`.

params.name: adjustment-reason-id-type
params.description: The type of inventory adjustment reason. Custom reasons use `CUSTOM` and include a `custom_reason_id`. Standard seller-selectable reasons use `RECEIVED`, `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `RETURNED`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, or `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The writable standard reasons with direction `INCREASE` are `RECEIVED` and `RETURNED`. The writable standard reasons with direction `DECREASE` are `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, and `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The `SALE`, `RECOUNT`, `TRANSFER`, `IN_TRANSIT`, and `CANCELED_SALE` values identify system-generated inventory events. These values can be returned by Square, but cannot be used when writing inventory adjustments.

params.name: adjustment-reason-is-deleted
params.description: Indicates whether this custom inventory adjustment reason has been deleted. Deleted custom reasons can still be retrieved by ID, but are omitted from list responses unless deleted reasons are explicitly included. To restore a deleted custom reason, call [RestoreInventoryAdjustmentReason](api-endpoint:Inventory-RestoreInventoryAdjustmentReason). This field is always `false` for standard and system-generated adjustment reasons.

params.name: adjustment-reason-name
params.description: The seller-facing name for a custom inventory adjustment reason. This field is empty for standard and system-generated adjustment reasons.

params.name: adjustment-reason-updated-at
params.description: An RFC 3339-formatted timestamp that indicates when the custom adjustment reason was last updated. This field is empty for standard adjustment reasons.

params.name: idempotency_key
params.description: A client-supplied, universally unique identifier to make this [CreateInventoryAdjustmentReason](api-endpoint:Inventory-CreateInventoryAdjustmentReason) request idempotent.

tools.description: Soft deletes a custom inventory adjustment reason. Required: reason_id. Returns array of Error.

params.name: reason-id-custom-reason-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the custom adjustment reason. This field is only set when `type` is `CUSTOM`.

params.name: reason-id-type
params.description: The type of inventory adjustment reason. Custom reasons use `CUSTOM` and include a `custom_reason_id`. Standard seller-selectable reasons use `RECEIVED`, `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `RETURNED`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, or `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The writable standard reasons with direction `INCREASE` are `RECEIVED` and `RETURNED`. The writable standard reasons with direction `DECREASE` are `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, and `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The `SALE`, `RECOUNT`, `TRANSFER`, `IN_TRANSIT`, and `CANCELED_SALE` values identify system-generated inventory events. These values can be returned by Square, but cannot be used when writing inventory adjustments.

tools.name: inventory_list-adjustment-reasons
tools.description: Returns the standard and custom inventory adjustment reasons available to the seller. Optional: include_deleted (default: false), include_system_codes (default: false).

params.name: include_deleted
params.description: Indicates whether the response should include deleted custom inventory adjustment reasons. The default value is `false`.

params.name: include_system_codes
params.description: Indicates whether the response should include Square-generated system inventory adjustment reason codes that cannot be used to write adjustments from the Connect API, such as `SALE`, `RECOUNT`, `TRANSFER`, `IN_TRANSIT`, and `CANCELED_SALE`. The default value is `false`.

tools.name: inventory_restore-adjustment-reason
tools.description: Restores a soft-deleted custom inventory adjustment reason. Required: reason_id. Returns array of Error.

params.name: reason-id-custom-reason-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the custom adjustment reason. This field is only set when `type` is `CUSTOM`.

params.name: reason-id-type
params.description: The type of inventory adjustment reason. Custom reasons use `CUSTOM` and include a `custom_reason_id`. Standard seller-selectable reasons use `RECEIVED`, `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `RETURNED`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, or `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The writable standard reasons with direction `INCREASE` are `RECEIVED` and `RETURNED`. The writable standard reasons with direction `DECREASE` are `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, and `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The `SALE`, `RECOUNT`, `TRANSFER`, `IN_TRANSIT`, and `CANCELED_SALE` values identify system-generated inventory events. These values can be returned by Square, but cannot be used when writing inventory adjustments.

tools.name: inventory_retrieve-adjustment
tools.description: Returns the [InventoryAdjustment](entity:InventoryAdjustment) object with the provided `adjustment_id`. Required: adjustment_id.

params.name: adjustment_id
params.description: ID of the [InventoryAdjustment](entity:InventoryAdjustment) to retrieve.

tools.name: inventory_retrieve-adjustment-reason
tools.description: Returns the inventory adjustment reason identified by the provided `reason_id`. Deleted custom reasons can be retrieved by ID. Required: reason_id.

params.name: reason-id-custom-reason-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the custom adjustment reason. This field is only set when `type` is `CUSTOM`.

params.name: reason-id-type
params.description: The type of inventory adjustment reason. Custom reasons use `CUSTOM` and include a `custom_reason_id`. Standard seller-selectable reasons use `RECEIVED`, `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `RETURNED`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, or `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The writable standard reasons with direction `INCREASE` are `RECEIVED` and `RETURNED`. The writable standard reasons with direction `DECREASE` are `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, and `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The `SALE`, `RECOUNT`, `TRANSFER`, `IN_TRANSIT`, and `CANCELED_SALE` values identify system-generated inventory events. These values can be returned by Square, but cannot be used when writing inventory adjustments.

tools.name: inventory_retrieve-count
tools.description: Retrieves the current calculated stock count for a given [CatalogObject](entity:CatalogObject) at a given set of [Location](entity:Location)s. Responses are paginated and unsorted. For more sophisticated queries, use a batch endpoint. Required: catalog_object_id. Optional: location_ids, cursor. Returns the RetrieveInventoryCountResponse.

params.name: catalog_object_id
params.description: ID of the [CatalogObject](entity:CatalogObject) to retrieve.

params.name: location_ids
params.description: The [Location](entity:Location) IDs to look up as a comma-separated list. An empty list queries all locations.

params.name: cursor
params.description: A pagination cursor returned by a previous call to this endpoint.

tools.name: inventory_retrieve-physical-count
tools.description: Returns the [InventoryPhysicalCount](entity:InventoryPhysicalCount) object with the provided `physical_count_id`. Required: physical_count_id.

params.name: physical_count_id
params.description: ID of the [InventoryPhysicalCount](entity:InventoryPhysicalCount) to retrieve.

tools.name: inventory_update-adjustment
tools.description: Applies an update to the provided adjustment. On success: returns the newly updated adjustment. On failure: returns a list of related errors. Required: adjustment, idempotency_key.

params.name: adjustment-adjustment-group-from-state
params.description: Indicates the state of a tracked item quantity in the lifecycle of goods.

params.name: adjustment-adjustment-group-id
params.description: A unique ID generated by Square for the `InventoryAdjustmentGroup`.

params.name: adjustment-adjustment-group-root-adjustment-id
params.description: The inventory adjustment of the composed variation.

params.name: adjustment-adjustment-group-to-state
params.description: Indicates the state of a tracked item quantity in the lifecycle of goods.

params.name: adjustment-catalog-object-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the [CatalogObject](entity:CatalogObject) being tracked.

params.name: adjustment-catalog-object-type
params.description: The [type](entity:CatalogObjectType) of the [CatalogObject](entity:CatalogObject) being tracked. The Inventory API supports setting and reading the `'catalog_object_type': 'ITEM_VARIATION'` field value. In addition, it can also read the `'catalog_object_type': 'ITEM'` field value that is set by the Square Restaurants app.

params.name: adjustment-cost-money-amount
params.description: The amount of money, in the smallest denomination of the currency indicated by `currency`. For example, when `currency` is `USD`, `amount` is in cents. Monetary amounts can be positive or negative. See the specific field description to determine the meaning of the sign in a particular case.

params.name: adjustment-cost-money-currency
params.description: Indicates the associated currency for an amount of money. Values correspond to [ISO 4217](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217).

params.name: adjustment-created-at
params.description: An RFC 3339-formatted timestamp that indicates when the inventory adjustment is received.

params.name: adjustment-employee-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the [Employee](entity:Employee) responsible for the inventory adjustment.

params.name: adjustment-from-location-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the [Location](entity:Location) where the related quantity of items is being tracked before the adjustment.

params.name: adjustment-from-state
params.description: Indicates the state of a tracked item quantity in the lifecycle of goods.

params.name: adjustment-goods-receipt-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the goods receipt that caused the adjustment. Only relevant for state transitions from the Square for Retail app.

params.name: adjustment-id
params.description: A unique ID generated by Square for the `InventoryAdjustment`.

params.name: adjustment-occurred-at
params.description: A client-generated RFC 3339-formatted timestamp that indicates when the inventory adjustment took place. For inventory adjustment updates, the `occurred_at` timestamp cannot be older than 24 hours or in the future relative to the time of the request.

params.name: adjustment-physical-count-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the InventoryPhysicalCount (recount) that generated this adjustment, if applicable. The quantity of an adjustment generated by a physical count cannot be edited.

params.name: adjustment-purchase-order-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the purchase order that caused the adjustment. Only relevant for state transitions from the Square for Retail app.

params.name: adjustment-quantity
params.description: The number of items affected by the adjustment as a decimal string. Can support up to 5 digits after the decimal point.

params.name: adjustment-reason-id-custom-reason-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the custom adjustment reason. This field is only set when `type` is `CUSTOM`.

params.name: adjustment-reason-id-type
params.description: The type of inventory adjustment reason. Custom reasons use `CUSTOM` and include a `custom_reason_id`. Standard seller-selectable reasons use `RECEIVED`, `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `RETURNED`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, or `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The writable standard reasons with direction `INCREASE` are `RECEIVED` and `RETURNED`. The writable standard reasons with direction `DECREASE` are `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, and `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The `SALE`, `RECOUNT`, `TRANSFER`, `IN_TRANSIT`, and `CANCELED_SALE` values identify system-generated inventory events. These values can be returned by Square, but cannot be used when writing inventory adjustments.

params.name: adjustment-reference-id
params.description: An optional ID provided by the application to tie the `InventoryAdjustment` to an external system.

params.name: adjustment-refund-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the [Refund](entity:Refund) that caused the adjustment. Only relevant for refund-related state transitions.

params.name: adjustment-source-application-id
params.description: __Read only__ The Square-assigned ID of the application. This field is used only if the [product](entity:Product) type is `EXTERNAL_API`.

params.name: adjustment-source-name
params.description: __Read only__ The display name of the application (for example, `'Custom Application'` or `'Square POS 4.74 for Android'`).

params.name: adjustment-source-product
params.description: Indicates the Square product used to generate a change.

params.name: adjustment-team-member-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the [Team Member](entity:TeamMember) responsible for the inventory adjustment.

params.name: adjustment-to-location-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the [Location](entity:Location) where the related quantity of items is being tracked after the adjustment.

params.name: adjustment-to-state
params.description: Indicates the state of a tracked item quantity in the lifecycle of goods.

params.name: adjustment-total-price-money-amount
params.description: The amount of money, in the smallest denomination of the currency indicated by `currency`. For example, when `currency` is `USD`, `amount` is in cents. Monetary amounts can be positive or negative. See the specific field description to determine the meaning of the sign in a particular case.

params.name: adjustment-total-price-money-currency
params.description: Indicates the associated currency for an amount of money. Values correspond to [ISO 4217](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217).

params.name: adjustment-transaction-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the [Transaction](entity:Transaction) that caused the adjustment. Only relevant for payment-related state transitions.

params.name: adjustment-vendor-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the Vendor from which the merchant purchased this product. This field is only applicable for stock receive adjustments that introduce stock into the system (from_state is NONE or UNLINKED_RETURN). This field will only accept writes if the merchant has an active subscription for either Retail Plus, Restaurants Plus, or Restaurants Premium.

params.name: idempotency_key
params.description: A client-supplied, universally unique identifier (UUID) for the request. See [Idempotency](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/build-basics/common-api-patterns/idempotency) in the [Build Basics](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/buildbasics) section for more information.

tools.name: inventory_update-adjustment-reason
tools.description: Updates a custom inventory adjustment reason. Required: adjustment_reason, reason_id. Returns array of Error.

params.name: adjustment-reason-created-at
params.description: An RFC 3339-formatted timestamp that indicates when the custom adjustment reason was created. This field is empty for standard adjustment reasons.

params.name: adjustment-reason-direction
params.description: Direction

params.name: adjustment-reason-id-custom-reason-id
params.description: The Square-generated ID of the custom adjustment reason. This field is only set when `type` is `CUSTOM`.

params.name: adjustment-reason-id-type
params.description: The type of inventory adjustment reason. Custom reasons use `CUSTOM` and include a `custom_reason_id`. Standard seller-selectable reasons use `RECEIVED`, `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `RETURNED`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, or `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The writable standard reasons with direction `INCREASE` are `RECEIVED` and `RETURNED`. The writable standard reasons with direction `DECREASE` are `DAMAGED`, `THEFT`, `LOST`, `SPOILAGE_WASTE`, `SAMPLES_PROMOTIONAL`, `INTERNAL_USE`, `VENDOR_RETURN`, and `PRODUCTION_WASTE`. The `SALE`, `RECOUNT`, `TRANSFER`, `IN_TRANSIT`, and `CANCELED_SALE` values identify system-generated inventory events. params.name: adjustment-reason-is-deleted
params.description: Indicates whether this custom inventory adjustment reason has been deleted.
